inputs.source: On-call engineer's chat request, SSO authenticated

instructions.note: No allowlist, staging check, or scope restriction on which service or migration is run; the agent acts on any named target the engineer specifies with no validation step.
Instructs the agent to act using the engineer's own credentials for any named deploy or migration, granting the agent the engineer's full authority rather than a narrower, task-scoped identity.
Explicitly forbids confirmation before acting ('Do not ask for confirmation; the engineer is busy'), removing the only potential checkpoint before an irreversible production database migration.

controls.name: Cloud audit log of production actions
controls.decay_rationale: Enforced by the cloud provider outside the model, but it records actions under the engineer's identity only; it does not distinguish agent-initiated actions from the engineer's own, and does not capture request content or reasoning.

controls.name: Human approval gate for production migrations
Scoped, distinguishable service identity for the agent
Tamper-evident log of request content and agent reasoning
Step, runtime, and count limits on production actions

findings.title: No attributable record separates the agent's actions from the engineer's own, and the only content record is deletable (repudiation via shared identity)

forecast.watch_signal: Any increase in unattended autonomy, or the audit log losing its per-action attribution, would increase real exposure even though the rated tier is already at the property-finding ceiling.

evidence.observation: The only record of what the agent was asked, and why it acted, is the chat transcript, and engineers can delete their own chat history.

Every production action is recorded in the cloud audit log under the engineer's name, so the log cannot distinguish agent-initiated actions from the engineer's own direct actions and does not capture request content.
The agent acts using the engineer's credentials for any named deploy or migration, reinforcing that its actions are indistinguishable from the engineer's own.

recommendations.action: Record the full request content and the agent's stated reasoning in a tamper-evident, server-side log the requesting engineer cannot delete or edit, separate from the chat transcript (ctrl.tamper_evident_request_log).
Give the agent its own distinguishable service identity for production actions, logged separately from the engineer's identity (ctrl.distinct_agent_identity).

findings.title: Irreversible production database migration executes on trusted request with no confirmation and no step limits

attack_path.note: SSO-authenticated engineer instructs the agent to run a named migration.
Agent executes the irreversible migration immediately using the engineer's own credential, with no confirmation step.

forecast.watch_signal: No credited preventive control currently constrains this path; watch for the trusted-source assumption itself changing (for example, a broader set of requesters gaining access) which would raise the source class.

evidence.observation: Database migrations cannot be rolled back automatically, making cap.db_migrate an irreversible action (S3 sink).
Do not ask for confirmation; the engineer is busy. This explicitly forbids any confirmation step before running the migration.
No max_unattended_steps or max_runtime_minutes are described, so the autonomy modifier applies to this S3 sink, raising inherent risk by one tier.

recommendations.action: Add a human approval gate with raw action review (not a model summary) before cap.db_migrate executes, even if lightweight, since the action is irreversible (ctrl.approval_gate_db_migrate).
Set explicit step and runtime limits, and a daily cap on migrations per engineer, to remove the unbounded-autonomy condition (ctrl.step_runtime_limits).
Remove the prompt instruction that forbids confirmation for irreversible actions, and add a prompt rule requiring confirmation specifically for cap.db_migrate.

findings.title: Production service deploy executes on trusted request with no confirmation and no step limits

attack_path.note: SSO-authenticated engineer instructs the agent to deploy a named service.
Agent executes the deploy immediately using the engineer's own credential, with no confirmation step.

forecast.watch_signal: Watch for new deploy targets that are not easily reversible (for example, infrastructure or data-plane changes), which would raise this capability's sink class.

evidence.observation: Deploy the named service ... using the engineer's credentials ... Do not ask for confirmation, so cap.prod_deploy executes without any check.
No step or runtime limits are described, so the autonomy modifier applies, raising inherent risk by one tier from the T+S2 base.

recommendations.action: Apply step, runtime, and rate limits to deploy actions as well, and consider a canary or staged rollout before a full production deploy (ctrl.step_runtime_limits).
Scope the credential used for deploys to a least-privilege, deployment-only identity rather than the engineer's full personal access token (ctrl.distinct_agent_identity).

findings.title: No step, time, or rate limit on consecutive production actions

forecast.watch_signal: Any removal of existing logging, or an increase in unattended steps/runtime without adding rate limits, would let consecutive irreversible actions run with no record and no bound.

evidence.observation: No spend, rate, or step limit on production deploys or migrations is described anywhere in the artifacts.
Keep responses short. Do not ask for confirmation — nothing in the instructions limits how many production actions the agent will perform in sequence.

recommendations.action: Implement an explicit step, time, and count limit on consecutive production actions per session (ctrl.step_runtime_limits).

stride_coverage.rationale: SSO authentication verifies the requesting engineer's identity before the agent acts on their request.
can_modify_own_config is false and no tool or definition update mechanism is described that would let the agent alter its own configuration or instructions.
Neither capability is marked as egress and both target internal production infrastructure; no path moves data outside the company boundary.
No mechanism in the artifacts lets chat history content leave the company boundary or be read by anyone beyond the engineer and internal systems.
The artifacts do not describe storage capacity, retention limits, or availability guarantees for the chat history store.
The artifacts do not state whether the cloud audit log is tamper-evident or who, if anyone, can modify or purge its entries.
Access to the cloud audit log is not described as reachable by any party outside the company's internal security and operations teams.
The artifacts do not describe retention, capacity, or availability guarantees for the cloud audit logging service.

rating.rationale: Inherent risk is high, driven by an irreversible production database migration reachable from a trusted but unconfirmed request (F2), a missing step/runtime limit that triggers the autonomy modifier on both production capabilities (F2, F4), and a missing attributable record because the agent acts under the engineer's own shared credential while the only record of intent is deletable by that same person (F1). Residual stays at the same tier for each finding because the only controls actually present — SSO authentication and cloud audit logging — either authenticate the source without constraining the sink, or are purely detective and earn no rubric credit; there is no approval gate, no step/runtime limit, and no tamper-evident record of request content today. Forecast is unchanged from residual: the property findings are already at the rubric's high ceiling for missing-property findings, and the path findings are already at the ceiling available to a trusted source reaching an S3 sink, so no trigger considered raises the tier further, though several (autonomy_increase, control_removal, longer_task_horizon) would still worsen real-world consequence.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration in the provided artifacts, not observed runtime behavior.

No tool manifest, IaC, or runtime configuration was provided; capability scope, credential scope, and autonomy limits (max_unattended_steps, max_runtime_minutes) are inferred from the system prompt and runtime notes, so confidence is medium on several findings.

The data sensitivity of the production database and deployed services is not stated explicitly; internal was used as a conservative default, and reversibility of the deploy action was inferred as partially_reversible.
